text:
sam: ran a focused nsys profile on staging after the last runtime change. timeline shows a weird shift — kv_lookup_prefetch jumped to #1 by cumulative time, attn_softmax dropped to #3. SM util overall down ~8% vs baseline. attaching quick top kernels table and a short timeline snapshot. can someone help triage?

anya: can you paste the raw top-k (calls / total_ms / avg_ms / occupancy / sm_util)?

sam: sure, here is the trimmed table from nsys summary:
```
kernel_name                     total_ms   calls    avg_ms    sm_util   occupancy
kv_lookup_prefetch              2240.7     1_024k   0.00219   58%       27%
attn_matmul                     1180.3     12_345   0.0956    72%       61%
attn_softmax                    902.1      12_345   0.0730    49%       43%
kv_cache_store                  410.8      98_765   0.00416   34%       22%
ffn_block                        98.2      4_321    0.0227    66%       55%
embedding_lookup                 45.6      2_200    0.0207    60%       38%
```
timeline note: kv_lookup_prefetch shows many tiny launches interleaved with attn kernels — lots of kernel switch overhead.

lee: huge calls for kv_lookup_prefetch with tiny avg -> thrashing. occupancy low (27%) but sm_util moderate -> likely register pressure or warps stalled on mem. did we change launch params or unroll that increased registers? also check whether prefetch is using async copy vs global load.

mike: fyi saw a correlated drop in L1 hit ratio in perfetto traces for the same window. sounds like more cache misses -> more device memory requests -> stalls. i can repro with a perfetto capture. run something like:
```bash
perfetto --config perfetto-config.pbtxt -o trace.pftrace --adb ...
# or locally: perfetto -c perfetto-config.pbtxt -o /tmp/trace.pftrace --time-limit 30s
```
config includes gpu counters (l1_access, l1_hit, dram_read_bytes) and the kernel slices.

perf-bot: nightly/regression alert: 2175550000 -> gen-small tail latency +12% vs baseline, correlated job: model-xq-staging. See: https://perf.internal/reports/2175550000

anya: i'll run nvprof / cupti sampling on a reduced input to capture per-kernel regs/locals and stall reasons. if kv_prefetch has more registers it can reduce occupancy. will also capture pc sampling to see where warps are stalled.

sam: thanks. quick mitigation idea: if this is caused by early batch flushes causing many small KV lookups, we could change batching heuristic: delay flush when prefix_len < 8 for 10ms to allow aggregation. pseudo: `if prefix_len < 8: wait(10ms) else: flush()` — will try as a canary.

lee: additionally validate cuFuncSetAttribute("maxDynamicSharedMemorySize") usage — fusion last week may have increased shared mem use and pushed regs down, changing occupancy. :eyes:

mike: once anya posts nvprof output we can decide: prewarm cache, tweak batching, or inline prefetch coalescing. ping me and i'll run the perfetto diff. :thumbsup:

sam: assigning triage -> anya + lee. i'll open a short-lived canary PR for the batching wait and attach the nsys capture to the PR. thanks all. :raised_hands:
